propositions: A bare fixture repository created with `git init --bare` runs git's default auto-maintenance after a push, spawning a detached background process that outlives the push and concurrently rewrites the object database.

The test's `shutil.copytree` immediately following a push races against that detached maintenance process, causing it to fail when it encounters loose-object fanout directories or maintenance.lock being pruned mid-walk.
Filtering `*.lock` from the copy does not eliminate the race because the actual mutator prunes entire loose-object directories during repack, not just lock files.

The fixture bare remote must be created with `receive.autogc=false`, `gc.autoDetach=false`, and `maintenance.autoDetach=false` pinned before any push, ensuring no detached background processes survive the push.

A new guard test asserts the absence of detached maintenance children by running the push under `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` and verifying no `git maintenance run` child carries `--detach`, with a `receive-pack` positive control to prevent vacuous passage.
